examples.title: Fire flow extension, L/s (SI)
examples.description: A new loop of 300 mm and 200 mm main tied into an existing system, which is a reservoir and a pump built from a hydrant flow test, in Johnson City, Texas. A fire hydrant junction passes 95 L/s with 14 m of residual pressure. Liters per second, with meters and millimeters.

examples.title: Fire flow extension, gpm (US)
examples.description: A new loop of 12 inch and 8 inch main tied into an existing system, which is a reservoir and a pump built from a hydrant flow test, in Johnson City, Texas. A fire hydrant junction passes 1,500 gpm with 20 psi of residual pressure. Gallons per minute, with feet and inches.

examples.title: Community well and tank, L/s (SI)
examples.description: A well pump with a check valve, a loop of 150 mm main, and a ground tank of 265 cubic meters on a single connection, with a 24-hour extended-period simulation, at the edge of Munday, Texas. A fire hydrant junction passes 32 L/s with 14 m of residual pressure. Liters per second, with meters and millimeters.

examples.title: Community well and tank, gpm (US)
examples.description: A well pump with a check valve, a loop of 6 inch main, and a ground tank of 67,000 gallons on a single connection, with a 24-hour extended-period simulation, at the edge of Munday, Texas. A fire hydrant junction passes 500 gpm with 20 psi of residual pressure. Gallons per minute, with feet and inches.

examples.title: EPANET Net3, L/s (SI)
examples.description: An EPANET example at Novato, California, converted from gallons per minute, feet, and inches, with the world map behind it: 92 junctions, 3 tanks, and 2 reservoirs, no valves, about 8 km square. A 24-hour extended-period simulation, with a source trace from the Lake. Liters per second, with meters and millimeters.

examples.title: EPANET Net3, gpm (US)
examples.description: An EPANET example at Novato, California, with the world map behind it: 92 junctions, 3 tanks, and 2 reservoirs, no valves, about 5 miles square. A 24-hour extended-period simulation, with a source trace from the Lake. Gallons per minute, with feet and inches.

examples.title: EPANET Net2, L/s (SI)
examples.description: An EPANET example at Branford, Connecticut, converted from gallons per minute, feet, and inches: 35 junctions and 1 tank, with no reservoir, no pump, and no valves, about 2 km by 4 km. Fluoride, a non-reactive substance, enters at one source. Liters per second, with meters and millimeters.

examples.title: EPANET Net2, gpm (US)
examples.description: An EPANET example at Branford, Connecticut: 35 junctions and 1 tank, with no reservoir, no pump, and no valves, about 1 mile by 2 miles. Fluoride, a non-reactive substance, enters at one source. Gallons per minute, with feet and inches.

examples.title: Elm Street Center, gpm (US)
examples.description: Prescott Valley, Arizona: 17 junctions, 1 reservoir, and 1 pump. A commercial site solved for fire flow on top of maximum day demand, at one moment in time, drawn over a site plan. Gallons per minute, with feet and inches.

examples.title: Valve types, gpm (US)
examples.description: A hilltop reservoir feeds a hub through a PBV, with a PRV, PSV, FCV, TCV, and GPV branching off it, each one controlling at the solved state. Gallons per minute, with feet and inches.

examples.title: EPANET Net1 with scenarios and rule-based controls, L/s (SI)
examples.description: Four scenarios under Base, the average day: Max day (demand multiplier 1.5) and Peak hour (2.25), each with a main break child, and the two children share one alternative. A fictional EPANET example, converted from gallons per minute, feet, and inches, with chlorine, 1 reservoir, 1 tank, 1 pump, and two rule-based controls. To test fire flow, make Max day current, select junction 23, choose Water, Analyze, Fire flow analysis, and enter a Required fire flow of 95 L/s.. Liters per second, with meters and millimeters.
